project-1.title: LiDAR Odometry & SLAM Stack
project-1.mainDescr: LiDAR odometry in C++ on KITTI: KISS-ICP-style scan-to-map registration, scored against ground truth and replayed live in an Open3D viewer.
project-1.description: I'm building this C++ pipeline to behave like a real sensor stack rather than a batch script. A producer thread replays KITTI LiDAR scans at their original timing into a fixed-size queue, so if the consumer falls behind, the reader waits instead of piling scans up in memory. Each scan is deskewed using velocities integrated from the OXTS data, then registered against a voxel hash map with KISS-ICP-style ICP: an adaptive correspondence threshold and Gauss-Newton updates, with the work split across a thread pool that stays alive between iterations. I score the trajectory against KITTI ground truth with relative pose error, plot the per-step translation and rotation error against the mean and RMSE in Python, and can watch a run in an Open3D viewer that shows the accumulated map, the raw scans or the dense map from several camera modes.

project-2.title: 3D Scene Reconstruction
project-2.mainDescr: My own NeRF in PyTorch, trained on the Blender LEGO scene. It scores 31.20 dB PSNR averaged over all 200 test views, trained in fp32 on a 6 GB laptop GPU.
project-2.description: Two ways of getting 3D out of 2D images. The first is a Structure-from-Motion pipeline that recovers camera poses and 3D points from ordinary photos: SIFT features, RANSAC, the fundamental and essential matrices, pose recovery, triangulation, PnP and bundle adjustment. The second is NeRF, which I implemented in PyTorch and trained on the synthetic LEGO scene to render it from new viewpoints. The current model reaches 31.20 dB PSNR and 0.9615 SSIM averaged over all 200 test views. It trained for 200,000 steps (about seven and a half hours) on my laptop's RTX 3060, all in fp32.

project-3.title: KITTI Semantic Segmentation
project-3.mainDescr: A UNet I wrote in PyTorch for pixel-wise semantic segmentation of KITTI street scenes, with scripts for training and inference.
project-3.description: Semantic segmentation of KITTI driving scenes with a UNet written from scratch in PyTorch. I wrote the dataset class with Albumentations augmentation, a training loop that tracks validation loss and mean IoU, and an inference script that saves side-by-side comparisons, overlays on the input image and colour-coded masks.

project-4.title: One-Shot Object Detection
project-4.mainDescr: Training YOLOv5n, YOLOv5s, YOLOv5m and YOLOv5l on a basketball image dataset I put together, and comparing them.
project-4.description: I trained four sizes of YOLOv5 (n, s, m and l) on a basketball image dataset I put together, and compared them across several train/test splits. The target is more than 85% average precision with the smallest one, YOLOv5n, on basketball video with several objects in frame and busy backgrounds.

project-5.title: Hybrid A*
project-5.mainDescr: A small Hybrid A* planner for ROS 2 that finds smooth, collision-free paths a car can actually drive. The planner is C++ and the visualization is Python.
project-5.description: A Hybrid A* planning package for ROS 2 Humble. One node publishes an occupancy map along with the start and goal poses. The C++ planner searches over position and heading using forward and reverse motion primitives, guided by a heuristic, and smooths the resulting path so it stays within the car's turning limits. A Python node then animates the planned path.

project-6.title: Trajectory Generation in Frenet Frame
project-6.mainDescr: Samples lateral and longitudinal polynomial paths in the Frenet frame, scores them and picks a collision-free one in real time. Everything is drawn with OpenCV and saved to video.
project-6.description: Trajectory planning in the Frenet frame, in C++. I build a reference path along the lane centre (x, y, yaw, curvature and arc length), then generate candidate trajectories: quintic polynomials for the lateral motion and quartic or quintic ones for the longitudinal motion, over several time horizons. Each candidate is scored on jerk, time and deviation from the centre line, and any that collide or break the kinematic limits are thrown out. The best one is converted back to world coordinates, and OpenCV draws all the candidates plus the chosen path and writes the result to trajectory.mp4.

project-7.title: EKF Localization
project-7.mainDescr: An Extended Kalman Filter tracking a simulated 4D unicycle, drawn live in OpenCV with a covariance ellipse that shrinks as the estimate settles. It can also save the animation as an MP4.
project-7.description: A C++ simulation for trying out an Extended Kalman Filter. The robot follows a three-part reference path (a sine wave, a straight run downwards, then a semicircle) while the program generates noisy odometry and position measurements, and the filter runs its predict and update steps in real time. The OpenCV view rescales itself to keep everything in frame and colour-codes the ground truth, odometry, observations and EKF estimate. A red covariance ellipse shrinks as the uncertainty drops. The animation can optionally be recorded to ekf_demo.mp4.

project-8.title: Atari Breakout DQN Agent
project-8.mainDescr: A Deep Q-Network (DQN) that learns to play Atari Breakout, trained with Stable-Baselines3 using frame stacking and my own preprocessing.
project-8.description: I wrapped the Breakout-v5 Gym environment with my own preprocessing (grayscale frames, frame skipping and a stack of the last four frames) and trained a Stable-Baselines3 DQN agent on it for 20 million timesteps on a GPU, tuning the hyperparameters along the way. An EvalCallback tracks progress and saves the best checkpoint during training, and Gym's RecordVideo wrapper records gameplay, so the videos show how the agent's play improves and what the final policy does.

project-9.title: Sliding Mode Control for Quadrotor
project-9.mainDescr: A sliding mode controller that makes a Crazyflie 2.0 track 3D polynomial trajectories in a Gazebo simulation.
project-9.description: I designed a sliding mode controller for a Crazyflie 2.0 quadrotor so it can follow 3D polynomial trajectories in Gazebo despite the nonlinear dynamics and external disturbances. The trajectories are 5th-order polynomials, and a control allocation matrix turns the controller output into rotor speeds, which are published to Gazebo in real time. The SMC gains are exposed as tuning parameters. Flight data is logged during each run, and a separate script plots the actual trajectory in 3D.

project-10.title: Travelling Salesman Problem
project-10.mainDescr: Python algorithms for the Travelling Salesman Problem, with a live plot of the route and an MP4 of the search.
project-10.description: A genetic algorithm in Python that finds short tours for the Travelling Salesman Problem. The first population is seeded with a greedy tour, and each generation uses elitism, roulette-wheel selection, ordered crossover and distance-based mutation. The parameters are easy to change. While it runs, Matplotlib shows the best route so far, and at the end it saves an MP4 of the route improving over the generations.

project-11.title: Joint Space Control of SCARA Arm
project-11.mainDescr: PID joint-space control for a SCARA arm in ROS, with an inverse kinematics solver that turns target positions into joint values.
project-11.description: Joint-space control for a SCARA manipulator in ROS. An inverse kinematics solver works out the joint values for a target position, and a PID controller drives each joint there. The code is split into ROS packages with service servers, publishers and subscribers, and the arm's motion and joint trajectories are plotted live.

project-12.title: Face Recognition/Verification Using Siamese Network
project-12.mainDescr: A face recognition system built around a Siamese network in TensorFlow.
project-12.description: Face recognition and verification with a Siamese network in TensorFlow, reaching at least 85% accuracy. I also implemented Google's FaceNet and a pre-trained random forest classifier to compare their accuracy with the Siamese network.

project-13.title: Automatic Camera Calibration
project-13.mainDescr: Camera calibration written from scratch in Python using Zhang's method: checkerboard detection, intrinsic and extrinsic estimation, and bundle adjustment.
project-13.description: I wrote camera calibration from scratch in Python using Zhang's method. It detects the checkerboard corners, estimates a homography for each image, solves for the intrinsic and extrinsic parameters, models radial distortion and then refines everything with nonlinear bundle adjustment. I made plots to check each step and compared the final calibration with OpenCV's, getting sub-pixel reprojection error.

description: Designed and deployed a real-time fused occupancy grid mapping system that combines ultrasonic (USS) and LiDAR data in the ego frame. It produces dense obstacle maps with few false positives for the motion planner, and it runs on production vehicles today.

Developed a zone-adaptive probabilistic mapping framework with spatial thresholds and temporal hit-count decay, so the map reacts faster to obstacles in critical driving zones while staying stable enough for the planner.
Built a LiDAR perception pipeline covering ego-time synchronization, motion compensation, voxelization and Patchwork++ ground segmentation, which outputs obstacle-only 2D point clouds for map fusion.
Implemented low-latency, real-time sensor fusion over RTI DDS that delivers time-synchronized occupancy maps on production vehicles.
Worked on refactoring legacy C++ code so it could orchestrate multi-arm welding, taking the system from a single robot to a four-arm cell.
Designed a modular resource management system in modern C++ (templates, smart pointers, std::optional, lambdas) that allocates and synchronizes shared resources across multiple robots.
Built test infrastructure with GMock, using inheritance-based mocks, and prototyped dependency injection to make the controllers easier to test.
Worked with the robotics and software teams to keep the system architecture in line with changing manufacturing requirements.
Used Git for version control and day-to-day collaboration across the development team.
Wrote Python automation tools for the Cubiscan 325 that cut warehouse management time by 70% and made product dimensioning more accurate for warehouse induction and packing.
Evaluated robotic motion planning, perception and application software with the development teams, helping tune each system and checking that it met its design specifications.
Wrote C++ modules and automated Google Test suites on Linux to extend an autonomous mobile robot's Nav2 setup in ROS2, working through Git in a CI/CD pipeline.
Built a mapping package that localizes an AMR outdoors by fusing high-precision Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) GPS, visual odometry from a ZED 2 camera and IMU data.
Integrated ROS2 for autonomous navigation, made the RViz C++ nodes for localization and mapping more reliable with Google Tests, and merged our custom localization with Nav2 and RViz visualization.

Wrote an Arduino sketch that connects Blynk with micro-ROS for extra robot functions, and moved the ROS2 Humble install from Docker to the Isaac ROS Buildfarm, which made the agent-client connection on the Jetson Orin more stable and simplified communication.

Built an MVP that inspects car chassis on a rotating platform, using a 6-DOF robot arm with a camera as its end effector. Written in C++ and Python, it automated precise, high-accuracy defect detection for automotive manufacturing.
Designed and built IoT systems for smart homes using PIR, ultrasonic, infrared, photodiode and thermostat sensors.
Built an automated defect detection system for conveyor belts with Cognex vision systems, OpenCV, C++ and Python, improving quality control and cutting errors by 40%.
Designed an automated sorting system that reads 1D and 2D barcodes and drives electric actuators, written in C++ and Python, which made sorting 60% more efficient.

bio:
I'm a perception software engineer at Lucid Motors, where I work on the real-time LiDAR and ultrasonic sensor fusion and occupancy mapping that runs on our production vehicles. Most of my work is in C++ and Python, across perception, sensor fusion, SLAM and motion planning, and I've used ROS and ROS2 on autonomous mobile robots and multi-robot systems.

I did my Master's in Robotics Engineering at Worcester Polytechnic Institute, where I focused on SLAM, path planning and robot perception. Before Lucid, I wrote multi-arm welding software for Path Robotics, worked on robotics software quality for Berkshire Grey, and built outdoor localization for an AMR at Void Robotics by fusing RTK GPS, visual odometry and an IMU. Before grad school, I spent several years building machine vision and automation systems at Nagarro Software and Automation Systems and Solution.
